# Retrospective: PR #12808

## What worked

Source-only inspection answered the material integration question without touching the live desktop. Following the new default app ID through unchanged terminal-tag and clipboard consumers exposed the important issue. Full independent reports preceded synthesis. Upstream xdg-terminal-exec source corrected an overbroad initial finding rather than allowing agreement or a migration comment to substitute for evidence. Both initial finals and the post-final addendum remain preserved.

## Deviations and correction

- Coordinator emitted more than 60 lines of owned registry metadata in one call. No technical conclusions were included. Subsequent state inspection projected selected fields and used bounded output.
- Opus reported an initial filename/count inventory of about 64 lines. It subsequently used bounded reads. No missing policy tails or runtime evidence resulted.
- Sol requested a 61-line source read during post-final adjudication. It retained the original history and reread the relevant source in 40/23-line chunks. This does not retroactively make the earlier call compliant.
- Fix for dispatch/tooling: aggregate metadata and source bounds must be implemented in each inventory, not only in prose. Prefer at most 40 inventory entries plus counts, and selected JSON fields. Use read limit <=60; count combined outputs before emission. These constraints were explicit in current dispatches but were not followed perfectly. Record this as instruction execution failure, not an omitted-rule excuse.
- Opus noted normal gh authentication/internal state was not individually write-audited; only explicit artifact destinations and notifier control were audited. No host test/config mutation was attempted or established. Do not claim complete utility-internal isolation for public-source fetch tooling.

## Independence and privacy

Fresh Opus 5.5 High and Sol Xhigh sessions verified. Opus autoMemoryEnabled=false was passed through supported session settings; startup project/process context and environment were disclosed, without prior technical conclusions. Pi received a fresh session/no resume and no persistent-memory tool. No intentional memory reads/writes. No peer finals read until both existed. Sol's addendum follows coordinator counterevidence after independence was complete, and is clearly labelled as such. Public draft contains no private artifact paths, identities, process/session IDs or infrastructure names.

## Evidence discipline

No runtime fixtures or broad test totals to rehabilitate. Retain only inspected pinned-source routing and corroborative external contracts. Native graphical behavior, installed versions, screensaver timing and migration execution remain untested. Failed public documentation fetches are retained. The suggested regex correction has not been executed.

## Resources and tooling

No desktop slots, namespaces, services or background test processes were created. Reviewer processes are cleaned by the coordinator through owned Herdr panes only, with receipts. No confirmed tool bug was found; the HTTP documentation failures are transport failures, not product defects. Avoid substitutes or extra tests when they cannot answer actual GUI questions under the assigned resources.

## Administrative cleanup receipt limitation

The first Claude Ctrl+D did not exit its completed session. After an explicit /exit, the successful cleaned-pane.json receipt inadvertently replaced the first still-active pane receipt at the same path. The original failed cleanup assertion remains in native coordinator history; it was not PR/runtime evidence. The final receipt independently confirms no agent remains in either owned reviewer pane. Future lifecycle attempts must use unique receipt names, just like test attempts. A failed editorial-copy attempt used a nonexistent source path and made no copy; it was retried using the recorded absolute check directory. No technical evidence or source was changed by either administrative error.

Source review found one clipboard integration issue in the newly supported default WezTerm launch.

### Ordinary WezTerm windows miss the terminal clipboard shortcuts

The normal Super+Return launcher does not override the app ID, so WezTerm uses `org.wezfurlong.wezterm`. The existing [terminal-tag rule](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/c77e26d7e055b5141be88248922a1a77cc171351/default/hypr/apps/terminals.lua#L1-L8) matches `wezterm`, not that full class. Without the `terminal` tag, [universal clipboard routing](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/c77e26d7e055b5141be88248922a1a77cc171351/default/hypr/bindings/clipboard.lua#L18-L46) takes the non-terminal branch:

| Shortcut | Intended terminal chord | Untagged WezTerm chord |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Super+C | Ctrl+Insert, copy | Ctrl+C |
| Super+V | Shift+Insert, paste | Ctrl+V |

This is a source-derived routing comparison, not an observed GUI test. The PR already binds the two Insert chords to WezTerm copy/paste, but ordinary default-class windows do not reach them. Explicitly classed `org.omarchy.*` windows are outside this finding.

**Impact:** Super+C can interrupt a foreground command instead of copying, and Super+V does not invoke the configured paste action.

**Suggested change:** Add `org\\.wezfurlong\\.wezterm` to the Lua regex in `default/hypr/apps/terminals.lua`, retaining `wezterm` if needed for other variants. The stale rule predates this PR, but the new supported default-terminal path exposes the mismatch.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source inspection at `c77e26d7e055b5141be88248922a1a77cc171351`, with upstream WezTerm/Hyprland source corroboration. No runtime tests, clipboard interaction, migration, theme/font reload, or multi-monitor screensaver validation was performed; installed package versions were not verified.

**Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Automated AI review:** Astra Medium initial inspection, independent Opus 5.5 High and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical reviews, then Astra Medium synthesis and source-based verification of the retained finding.
